title: Depth Anything: Unleashing the Power of Large-Scale Unlabeled Data
mechanism: With many labels, plain self-training gives nothing. It helps only with strong perturbation of the student's unlabelled inputs plus a 1-minus-cosine feature-alignment loss to a frozen DINOv2 (tolerance margin 0.85), applied to unlabelled images only, with the student re-initialised.
adaptation: House U-Net++ R34 student. Align layer3 output through a 1x1 projector (weight warmed up from 0 to 0.1) to frozen DINOv3 ViT-L or ConvNeXt-L stride-16 features of the same pool cell (1-channel image replicated to 3 channels). Margin 0.85, applied only to pool cells, plus colour/blur/CutMix on the student view.
min_experiment: Arm DA-feat (PF + pool pseudo-labels + strong perturbation + feature alignment) vs house PF, 5 seeds. Metrics: crack relF1@2, inactive IoU, E1 relF1@2. Kill if all are n.d.
evidence: R: 1.5M labelled + 62M unlabelled. Table 9 (ViT-L AbsRel): unlabelled without perturbation, no gain (KITTI 0.085 -> 0.085). With perturbation 0.081. Adding the feature loss 0.076. Gains on all 6 sets. Feature loss helps on unlabelled data, not on labelled. Margin 0.85 beats 1.0 (0.175 vs 0.188).
prior_overlap: Our Mean Teacher had no feature anchor and the same architecture as its teacher, which is exactly the failure case the paper describes. D24 #16 proposes feature alignment on labelled data; this version is on pool data with a margin. Open.
